transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-19
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 46m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Ava Morales (Redwood CSM); Rina Cho (Blueframe Head of ML), Marco Alvarez (Platform), Priya Singh (Data Eng), Tom Baker (SRE)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync to review pilot economics (tokens per dollar, tokens/sec, caching impact), discuss batching tradeoffs, and align on next steps for an extended benchmark and configuration handoff. Focus on reducing unit cost while keeping p95 latency in target.

Topics:
- Current tokens/sec and unit cost baseline
- KV/prefix cache observed savings and hit-rate variance
- Batching thresholds: latency vs throughput tradeoffs
- Model variants (q8 / q4) and quality/throughput tradeoffs
- Deployment mode discussion: hosted vs dedicated for steady traffic
- Next steps and owners

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — econ numbers, caching, batching, next steps. rina, how's the week going?
[00:20] Rina Cho: good, yep thanks. we ran the few tests you sent last night, um, saw some interesting spikes in the mid-length prompts — 200 to 400 tokens.
[00:34] Samir Patel: yeah so i'll kick us off with the numbers we pulled from the microbench. baseline (no cache, default batching) gave about 3,800 tokens per dollar on the hosted q8 variant, and tokens/sec averaged 45 for our synthetic worker profile. that's across 8 concurrent clients.
[01:05] Priya Singh: 3.8k tok/$ — that seemed higher than we expected, our internal estimate was 5k. were you including network egress and the encoder overhead?
[01:18] Samir Patel: good question. this is model-only compute cost on Redwood — doesn't include customer infra egress. we did include the tokenization + model time. if you include prefix caching, numbers change.
[01:35] Marco Alvarez: can you clarify prefix cache — are we using the KV cache package or the session-level context cache? sometimes our logs call it "K V cache" and it's confusing.
[01:52] Samir Patel: yep, thanks. it's the KV cache — the runtime's prefix K-V store where repeated system/prompt prefixes hit. think of it as prefix-level reuse, not long-term embeddings cache.
[02:10] Tom Baker: initial note — our SRE is nervous about warm-up behavior. we saw a p95 spike at the 8-minute mark during ramp.
[02:23] Samir Patel: we saw that in the trace — that's due to cold KV cache misses plus kernel JIT on the GPU. after the first 10k tokens the cache hit rate stabilized around 62% and p95 dropped ~110ms.
[02:45] Rina Cho: what's the cost delta with cache on vs off?
[02:52] Samir Patel: with KV cache enabled we saw an average tokens per dollar of ~6,200 on the same q8 run — so roughly a 63% improvement vs no-cache baseline for this prompt mix. but hit-rate swings between 38% and 77% depending on prompt variability — so your mileage depends on session stickiness.
[03:25] Priya Singh: 38% low end is concerning — which flows hit that low?
[03:31] Samir Patel: the low was during multi-turn chat where users changed topics frequently; system prompts changed often. single-turn API calls with stable system prompts were closer to 70%+.
[03:48] Jordan Lee: quick interjection — that suggests we should baseline two configs: interactive chat (low cache) and assistant-like flows (high cache). different batching thresholds probably too.
[04:02] Rina Cho: yes that matches our product split. next, batching: we tested continuous batching with dynamic thresholds. results?
[04:14] Samir Patel: continuous batching increased tokens/sec to ~78 in peak, so ~1.7x throughput improvement. however tail latency (p95) increased by ~12% for interactive 1-2 turn requests at the default 40ms batching window. with a 20ms window we got a better balance: 1.4x throughput, p95 under target.
[04:40] Tom Baker: that's the tradeoff — we can't exceed 220ms p95 on customer-facing queries. any batching config that pushes above that is a no-go.
[04:51] Samir Patel: agreed. on the hosted side we can set adaptive windows: aggressive batching for async high-throughput jobs, conservative for interactive routes.
[05:03] Marco Alvarez: curious about the quantized model variants — you mentioned q4 earlier. how stable is quality?
[05:12] Samir Patel: q4 is about 1.9x faster than q8 on the same hardware in our runs, tokens/sec jumps ~90 to 170 depending on seq len. quality drop is small on classification/rerank tasks but more noticeable on creative completions. Rina, you may want to run your eval prompts through q4 and q8 to see delta.
[05:38] Rina Cho: will do. our success metric is accuracy on the intent classifier > 95% and p95 latency < 220ms.
[05:48] Priya Singh: one ask — can you include tokenization variance in the next export? short tokens vs long tokens skew results a lot.
[05:58] Samir Patel: yes i'll add token-length buckets (0-100, 100-300, 300-800) in the sheet.
[06:08] Jordan Lee: has anyone tried dedicated capacity for steady traffic? the economics sometimes favor reserved for predictable workloads.
[06:17] Marco Alvarez: we looked at that band a bit internally — but committed infra is a procurement headache. still, if unit costs drop 30-40% on dedicated, procurement may greenlight it.
[06:31] Samir Patel: dedicated drops per-token compute by about 35% in our model but remember there's committed minimums and you lose some elasticity. we recommended hybrid: reserved pool for baseline plus hosted overspill.
[06:48] Tom Baker: security — if we move to dedicated or private, how does KMS/HSM integrate? we need key rotations and audit logs.
[06:58] Ava Morales: Redwood Private supports customer KMS + HSM integration, audit logs and SSO. we'll share SOC2 + security deck after this call.
[07:10] Rina Cho: please do, we need it for the vendor review.
[07:14] Jordan Lee: returning to caching: Marco, any chance you can run a 3-hour steady-state with KV cache enabled and a traffic mix that mirrors your production topic-switching? we'd like to see hit-rate over longer tail.
[07:27] Marco Alvarez: yes we can schedule that, probably Thursday night to not affect prod.
[07:33] Priya Singh: note — the cache TTL seems short in our test harness, might be evicting early. we'll check LRU thresholds.
[07:43] Samir Patel: good call — runtime allows tuning of cache size and LRU policy per model. i'll include recommended knobs in the handoff.
[07:55] Rina Cho: pricing question — are tokens/sec/$ numbers factoring batched amortization? sometimes we see per-request cost go down in batch, but per-interaction SLOs suffer.
[08:09] Samir Patel: tokens/sec/$ in our spreadsheet is a batch-aware metric: total tokens served per dollar over the interval. we also publish p95 latency per route so you can map tradeoffs.
[08:22] Jordan Lee: link to the sheet is in the meeting notes: https://redwood.example.com/s/blueframe-poc-benchmarks — Samir, please confirm you shared the version with the q4/q8 tabs.
[08:36] Samir Patel: shared; the sheet has tabs: baseline, cache-enabled, q4-vs-q8, batching-windows. small note: some column headers got truncated in export, sorry — will fix.
[08:47] Priya Singh: transcription aside, can we talk about warm-up? those JIT spikes — any mitigations?
[08:55] Samir Patel: twofold: pre-warm kernels and pre-populate KV cache by replaying last n prompts during bootstrap. for hosted we can do auto-warm on rollout; for private you'd run a short warm-up job.
[09:12] Tom Baker: are the warm-up ops charged as normal compute? that's fine but we want to account for it in cost model.
[09:20] Samir Patel: yes counted in the pilot. we'll include a 'warm-up amortization' line in the economics sheet.
[09:30] Rina Cho: anything else on throughput?
[09:33] Samir Patel: one more: continuous batching with smart routing — route long sequences to dedicated high-memory nodes and short interactive ones to low-latency nodes. net effect: higher overall tokens/sec and kept the p95 for interactive in target.
[09:50] Marco Alvarez: that routing logic — is it out-of-the-box or requires extra config?
[09:56] Samir Patel: it's policy-driven in Redwood. you set route rules by path/route and latency target. we can show a sample policy.
[10:04] Jordan Lee: ok recap time — Samir can you summarize the best config for Blueframe's two flow classes?
[10:12] Samir Patel: sure. Flow A (interactive): q8, KV cache enabled, conservative batching window 20ms, p95 target 220ms. Flow B (analytics/async): q4 or q8 depending on quality, aggressive batching 60-100ms, route to dedicated reserved pool if sustained throughput > X rps, enable KV cache where prompts are stable. I'll put exact numbers in the sheet.
[10:36] Priya Singh: can you include the tokens/sec/$ calc per flow and the expected monthly cost at our 1.2M tokens/day baseline?
[10:45] Samir Patel: yes — provisional numbers in sheet already, will expand with a monthly projection.
[10:52] Rina Cho: procurement wants a short blurb: why not just run everything q4 on hosted and save money?
[10:59] Samir Patel: q4 is tempting but quality regressions matter on some tasks. our recommendation: run q4 on non-critical/async pipelines and q8 on interactive/classification. also run A/B evals — we'll help set that up.
[11:16] Jordan Lee: any competitor notes from the team?
[11:19] Ava Morales: customers sometimes compare to OpenAI endpoints for simplicity and Pinecone for similarity search caching, but Redwood focuses on production economics + rollouts.
[11:30] Tom Baker: timeline — we're aiming to decide dedicated vs hosted by end of month. is that feasible?
[11:36] Jordan Lee: yes, if we get the 3-hour steady runs and the expanded sheet, we can model dedicated cost and decide.
[11:44] Rina Cho: ok that works.
[11:48] Samir Patel: final admin — i'll upload the updated sheet and a bench-run notebook to the shared folder and ping you. link again: https://redwood.example.com/s/blueframe-poc-benchmarks
[11:59] Marco Alvarez: thanks Samir.
[12:03] Jordan Lee: cool thanks all — quick recap of next steps then close.

Recap / explicit next steps (spoken):

[12:40] Jordan Lee: schedule 30m benchmark with Tom + Samir on 2026-09-22 10:00 PDT — Jordan will send invite.

Notes / caveats captured in call:
- Cache hit-rate variance means the 6k tok/$ number is not guaranteed for all flows; treat as conditional on hit-rate > 60%.
- q4 quality regressions need eval for creative completions; do not flip globally without A/B testing.
- Warm-up costs should be amortized in monthly billing; accounting will want that in procurement docs.
